summary: trailing_window(end, days) starts `days` days back, so a 7-day window covers 8 days
why_hard: churned() uses the identical-looking `timedelta(days=days)` and is CORRECT there; changing both breaks churn. Tests only see dashboard numbers.

summary: tile_of uses int(x / TILE), which truncates toward zero: negative coordinates land one tile too far right/up
why_hard: int() looks like the obvious way to get a tile index and all positive coordinates work; the inclusive ranges in render() look suspicious but are correct; round() and 'subtract 1 for negatives' are tempting but wrong.

summary: decide() returns all(results); for a resource kind with no rules, all([]) is True, so everyone is allowed
why_hard: all() reads naturally; the symptom is a 200 where a 403 is expected for kinds nobody configured. Adding rules for the kind, or raising for unknown kinds, are tempting but wrong.

summary: Luhn checksum doubles digits where i % 2 == 0 (including the check digit) instead of i % 2 == 1
why_hard: Needs exact knowledge of the Luhn algorithm; the parity test looks perfectly normal. The expiry check (month >= today.month) and the Mastercard range look suspicious but are correct.

summary: weighted_mean divides the weighted sum by count instead of total_weight
why_hard: 'sum / count' reads like a normal average and total_weight is computed right next to it; the shrink() formula looks odd but is correct; only the final rating/ranking is tested.

summary: Delete.undo re-inserts the removed text at self.end instead of self.start
why_hard: The crash is an IndexError raised in document.py (wrong file); clamping there hides the crash but the text stays scrambled. Move/Replace build on Delete, so several features break at once.

summary: setting() uses `.get(key) or DEFAULTS[key]`, so a deliberate override of 0 falls back to the default
why_hard: `x.get(k) or default` is a very common idiom; stock_level uses a look-alike `.get(sku, 0)` that is correct. Patching only the min_stock symptom leaves lead time wrong.

summary: The quoted-value regex uses greedy ".*", so a line with two quoted values swallows everything up to the last quote
why_hard: Lines with one quoted value parse fine; the damage shows up as wrong per-user error counts and messages in the report. Splitting on spaces is tempting but breaks values that contain spaces.

summary: parse_date reads DD/MM/YYYY bank dates with '%m/%d/%Y'; every day <= 12, so nothing crashes
why_hard: No crash and no docstring saying day-first; the expected months in the tests are the only clue. Patching month_key to use the day makes the monthly totals right but late-payment days stay wrong.

summary: parse_offset applies the sign only to the hours: '-03:30' becomes -150 minutes instead of -210
why_hard: Positive offsets, +05:45 and whole-hour negatives all work; only negative offsets with minutes break, and the symptom is meeting times in meetings.py. Two natural-looking rewrites are wrong for the other sign.

summary: get_order passes the query-string id (a str) to repo.find, which compares it with int ids, so nothing is ever found
why_hard: No exception: the str/int comparison is just False and the API answers 404. list_orders converts its parameter correctly, which hides the pattern. Comparing as strings in repo.find breaks ids with leading zeros.

summary: Prices are parsed with float(), so 3 x 2.675 becomes 8.0249999... and rounds half-up to 8.02 instead of 8.03
why_hard: money.py already uses Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP, so the rounding code looks careful and correct; the error is binary floating point entering earlier. The popular Decimal(str(x)) workaround in money.py does not fix it.

summary: RingBuffer.latest indexes start + count - i instead of start + count - 1 - i
why_hard: Once the buffer is full the wrong index silently returns the OLDEST entry instead of the newest (no None, no crash); append()'s modular arithmetic looks more suspicious than latest().

summary: line_of uses bisect_left instead of bisect_right, so an offset that is exactly a line start maps to the previous line
why_hard: Only problems at the very first character of a line get a wrong position; needs exact bisect semantics. line_starts uses `i + 1` and long_line adds MAX_LINE, both of which look off-by-one but are correct.

summary: The limit check uses `used is limit`, which is only True for small cached ints; at 1000 calls the team plan is not blocked
why_hard: `is` sits next to a legitimate `limit is UNLIMITED` sentinel check, and the free plan (100 calls) behaves correctly because CPython caches small ints. Only plans with limits above 256 fail.

summary: caret_upper treats ^0.x.y like ^1.x.y (`major > 0 or minor > 0`), so ^0.2.1 allows everything below 1.0.0 instead of below 0.3.0
why_hard: No crash, just a too-new version in the lockfile. The condition reads like 'anything except 0.0.x'; the fix needs the rule that a caret on 0.x locks the minor version. tilde_upper right next to it is correct, and every package at 1.0 or above resolves correctly.

summary: merge() extends the last interval to the new `end` instead of max(old end, end), so a short meeting inside a long one cuts the long one short
why_hard: Only nested intervals trigger it (a short block inside a long one); overlapping and touching blocks merge correctly. gaps() already uses max(cursor, end), which suggests the nesting case is handled.

summary: route() does not handle a destination with no road connection: prev[...] raises a plain KeyError instead of Unreachable
why_hard: The KeyError is caught by the report's `except KeyError` (UnknownCity subclasses KeyError), so the user sees a believable 'unknown city' message that points at parsing. plan_tour catches Unreachable, but nothing ever raises it. Catching KeyError in plan_tour instead also hides cities that really are unknown.

summary: stem() uses filename.rstrip('.csv'), which strips a SET of characters: 'jobs.csv' becomes 'job', 'metrics.csv' becomes 'metri'
why_hard: Correct for most names ('data.csv', 'Sales Q3.csv'); the symptom shows up as a misleading 'two inputs would both write ...' error from the clash check in pipeline.py. slug() uses .strip('_') correctly right next to it.

summary: Shared mutable state in two files: deep_merge updates DEFAULTS' nested dicts in place (and is not recursive), and load_config writes env overrides into the cached profile dict
why_hard: Two independent aliasing bugs with the same symptom (values leaking between loads). Fixing either one alone, or adding a deepcopy in only one place, leaves failing tests. Results depend on the order in which profiles are loaded.
